name: browser-control
description: Discover, connect to, and drive a real Chromium-based browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). General execute_cdp primitive, evaluate and navigate shortcuts, target discovery/routing, screenshot/PDF materialization, and cross-call CDP event polling.

operations.name: list_browsers
operations.description: List running Chromium-based browsers that have remote debugging enabled, with each one's live port.

operations.name: connect_browser
operations.description: Open and retain the browser-level CDP WebSocket. With no input it finds the live debugging port itself (never guess a port) and uses the preferred browser if one is set. browser picks one by name (chrome, beta, brave) and opens it if it is not running. Idempotent while connected. Asking for a different browser keeps the current connection open in the background, so switching back needs no new Allow prompt.

operations.name: disconnect_browser
operations.description: Close every retained CDP socket and clear the active route and event buffer. Rarely needed: reconnecting costs the user another Allow prompt.

operations.name: get_browser_status
operations.description: Report connection, active target routing, buffered event count, and the artifact directory.

operations.name: list_targets
operations.description: Enumerate CDP targets (tabs, out-of-process iframes, workers). Internal chrome:// and devtools:// URLs are hidden unless includeAll is set.

operations.name: select_target
operations.description: Attach to a target (flattened) and route subsequent target-scoped execute_cdp calls to it. Changes the single active route.

operations.name: clear_target
operations.description: Detach routing so target-scoped calls no longer auto-route.

operations.name: close_target
operations.description: Close an agent-opened tab on the extension backend. Refuses tabs Browser Control did not open. With no targetId, closes the active extension tab.

operations.name: execute_cdp
operations.description: Call any Chrome DevTools Protocol method (Domain.command) and return its raw result. Browser.*, Target.*, and Extensions.* go to the browser endpoint; other methods route to the active target unless sessionId or targetId is given.

operations.name: evaluate
operations.description: Run JavaScript in the page and return its value directly. Top-level await works, promises are awaited, and const/let can be re-declared between calls. A thrown error fails with JS_EXCEPTION. Wraps Runtime.evaluate.

operations.name: navigate
operations.description: Navigate the target to a URL and wait for its load event (or, with until:"domcontentloaded", only until the document is parsed). loaded:false means the page was still loading at timeoutMs (default 30000); a failed navigation is an error. Wraps Page.navigate.

operations.name: capture_screenshot
operations.description: Capture a page screenshot and write it to a file (path, or a unique file in the artifact directory), returning the path, MIME type, and byte size. Wraps Page.captureScreenshot.

operations.name: capture_pdf
operations.description: Render the current page to a PDF file (path, or a unique file in the artifact directory), returning the path and byte size. Wraps Page.printToPDF.

operations.name: read_events
operations.description: Drain buffered CDP events collected across operations, optionally filtered by method, target, or session. Events only arrive after the relevant domain is enabled via execute_cdp.

operations.name: wait_for_event
operations.description: Wait until the next CDP event matching a method (and optional shallow params subset) arrives, or until timeout. A timeout is a normal found:false result, not an error.

config.notes: No credentials. The browser must have remote debugging enabled and must have granted the connection (chrome://inspect#remote-debugging, click Allow). All variables are optional overrides.

state.location: BROWSER_ARTIFACT_DIR or the OS temp directory (browser-control/)
state.notes: No durable capability state. The CDP connection, active target route, and bounded event buffer live in-process and are released by dispose(). Durable browser state (tabs, cookies, storage) lives in the browser, not here; screenshots/PDFs are written to an absolute artifact directory.
